issues.description: The problem specification and UML require Animal.messageOnFeed() to be abstract and to return a String, but the reference solution changes the return type to FeedResponse. This divergence (solution: FeedResponse vs. specification/template: String) is a structural mismatch that can confuse students about the expected signature and type to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of messageOnFeed() consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to have Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (and have subclasses return the message String), or (B) update the problem statement and UML to specify FeedResponse as the return type and document the FeedResponse class. Prefer (A) if the exercise intends to teach basic polymorphism with simple String messages; prefer (B) only if FeedResponse is intentionally part of the design and then update the template, UML, and instructions accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies an abstract method messageOnFeed() that returns a String, but the solution changes the method to return a FeedResponse object and introduces a new FeedResponse class. This alters the expected signature/type of the same conceptual method and may confuse students mapping the requirement (messageOnFeed(): String) to the provided solution (messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either change the solution to have Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (and have Pig/Seal/Goat return String messages), or update the problem statement and template to accept/describe a FeedResponse return type and document the FeedResponse class. Preferably revert to messageOnFeed(): String to match the exercise description and keep the API simple for students.
